review_evidence: README describes neural-network programming and formal reasoning in one Lean project, with tensor shapes in types and shared definitions used by training, graph transformations, certificate checkers, and proofs.
The hydrated source contains 1248 Lean files and 2618 proposition declarations, far beyond ordinary runtime/backend scaffolding.
Its mathematical meaning, assumptions, graph transformations, verification paths, and proof corpus are substantive formalization prior art.
summary: Retain TorchLean as a large formal neural-network library with executable tensors, proof interfaces, certificate checkers, and mathematical semantics.

summary: This is a re-review of the entire lean-dojo__TorchLean source (prior review RRV-298c1e5a1620-r1 retained the whole library; since then 1415 of 1459 .lean files changed or were added, 436 were removed). Surveyed the full current checkout: top-level dirs NN/ (1395 .lean files across API, Backend, CI, Core, Data, Examples, Floats, GraphSpec, IR, MLTheory, Proofs, Runtime, Spec, Tactic, Tensor, Testing, Tests, Verification, Widgets), home_page/blueprint/ (59 .lean files, a Verso documentation book mixing prose/LaTeX with embedded Lean definitions), and scripts/checks/TorchLeanLint.lean (1 file). No non-.lean files (CITATION.cff, formalization.yaml, lake-manifest.json, lean-toolchain, LICENSE, README.md) are in this unit's scope. Ran a whole-word grep for theorem|lemma|def|structure|class|instance|inductive|abbrev|example|axiom across the checkout; 164 files matched none of these keywords (grouped: 34 NN/Runtime, 17 NN/Tensor, 16 NN/Proofs, 16 NN/API, 14 NN/MLTheory, 13 NN/Spec, 11 NN/Examples, 10 NN/Verification, 6 NN/Tactic, 5 NN/CI, 4 NN/GraphSpec, 4 NN/Floats, 2 home_page/blueprint, 1 each NN/Tests, NN/Testing, NN/Data, plus 8 top-level umbrella files NN.lean/NN/API.lean/NN/Backend.lean/NN/Floats.lean/NN/IR.lean/NN/MLTheory.lean/NN/Spec.lean/NN/Tactic.lean). Read a representative sample of 25 of these 164 files spanning every listed subdirectory group in full. This grep keyword list is a heuristic, not a definitive import-only test: it does not recognize `opaque`, `macro`/`macro_rules`, `attribute [...]`, `add_aesop_rules`, or `syntax`, so several flagged files turned out to hold real declarations under those forms rather than being import-only. Read in full: home_page/blueprint/TorchLeanBlueprint.lean, home_page/blueprint/TorchLeanBlueprint/FormalizationMap.lean (both pure-import umbrellas); NN/Tactic/Autograd.lean (attribute/aesop-rule wiring plus `macro "autograd"`/`macro "autograd?"` custom tactic definitions -- genuine tactic infrastructure); NN/Runtime/Autograd/Engine/Cuda/ConvPool.lean (9 `opaque` FFI declarations with `extern` attributes -- genuine FFI bindings); NN/Testing/Command.lean (defines a `syntax`/`macro_rules` differential-test command `#compare`); NN/Tests/Tensor/EinsumPlanning.lean (real `#guard` executable regression assertions on einsum tiling logic); scripts/checks/TorchLeanLint.lean (real `def runChecked` and other lint-driver definitions, module-header only in the grep's blind spot due to comment-heavy preamble -- actually contains defs, sampled for directory coverage); and 17 further files (NN/API.lean, NN/Backend.lean, NN.lean, NN/CI/All.lean, NN/Floats.lean, NN/GraphSpec/Core.lean, NN/MLTheory.lean, NN/Proofs/Verification.lean, NN/Spec.lean, NN/Tensor.lean, NN/Verification/Cert.lean, NN/IR.lean, NN/Data/IO.lean, NN/Runtime/RL.lean, NN/Runtime/RL/Boundary.lean, NN/Examples/Models/RL.lean, plus NN/Widgets/Core/UI.lean sampled outside the grep hit-set for directory coverage) each confirmed to follow the same documented pure-import umbrella pattern (copyright header, `module`, `public import` list, `/-! # ... -/` doc comment describing the subsystem, `@[expose] public section`), or, for NN/Widgets/Core/UI.lean, genuine widget-helper code with real `def`s. Also read the opening of home_page/blueprint/TorchLeanBlueprint/Guide/Ch1_Introduction/Motivation.lean (881 lines, a Verso `#doc (Manual)` chapter mixing prose/math exposition with real embedded `def` declarations, e.g. `def moScores`), and the header of NN/MLTheory/Proofs/ReLU/Approximation/CompactSet.lean (the largest file in the checkout at 85540 bytes, a genuine ReLU-universal-approximation theorem file citing Stone-Weierstrass). Listed and reviewed the full NN/Examples directory tree (BugZoo/, Data/, DeepDives/, Factorization/, Functional/, Interop/, Models/, Optimization/, Quickstart/, Runner*.lean, Support/, Verification.lean) -- these are TorchLean's own worked-example/tutorial Lean modules, not vendored fixtures or generated dumps. No file examined in this unit is a generated data table, LLM transcript dump, vendored copy, placeholder stub, or non-Lean binary artifact.
